Albany seeks out [nation]Pantagruel[/nation] with an offer of a comprehensive pact of recognition, commerce, and cooperation, framed to strengthen both nations positions in the modern world. We extend this proposal in good faith, convinced that both of our peoples will prosper more together than apart, and that the stability born from recognition and open exchange shall serve us well in the decades to come.

First, we affirm that each shall recognize the full legitimacy of the others state, government, borders, and laws. It is vital that disputes of the past remain settled, that borders be considered final and inviolable, and that jurisdiction remain exclusive within each sovereign land. All outstanding questions from previous decades are to be resolved by this affirmation, so that neither of us is left uncertain as to what belongs to whom.

We suggest that each establish embassies in the others capital and maintain direct lines of communication between foreign ministries. Beyond this, consulates may be created in proportion to the commerce flowing between us. This ensures balance while providing space for community outreach and cultural contact, for what is diplomacy if not also the friendship of peoples?

Trade should flow openly, yet fairly. Tariffs ought not to exceed five percent on any good, and ideally much lower where possible. We believe manufactured goods, technology, and services can be limited to three percent tariffs, while critical raw resources such as coal, lithium, uranium, iron, and rare earths can bear no more than two percent. This ensures that each has access to what it needs at fair rates, without one party unduly profiting from duties. Reductions should also follow a principle of equalization, such that they scale in line with each economys growth. Where exemptions are required to protect vulnerable industries, they shall be time-limited and subject to review every three years by a joint commission seated alternately in our courts and their commercial registry.

Resources are the lifeblood of prosperity. Here we suggest that each grant the other the right of first purchase over surplus uranium, lithium, and iron, at prevailing market rates, with minimum export allotments secured before trade with third parties. Refining and processing industries, being costly and complex, shall be sited where geography and efficiency best serve global markets, ensuring neither of us is disadvantaged. Shared pipelines and storage shall operate according to the laws of the transit state, so that governance is clear and disputes avoided. For offshore zones, both of us should extend mutual recognition of Exclusive Economic Zones to two hundred nautical miles, yet where overlap exists, shared exploitation zones should be governed by the domestic law of the state with the larger onshore administrative capacity, so that resources do not go untapped.

Agriculture and food security must not be overlooked. Food tariffs should be entirely eliminated, and each of us must pledge that shortages will never be allowed to afflict the other if supply can be ensured. Agricultural exports should meet domestic demand in both nations, with shortages alleviated as a priority. Standards of safety and quality may be harmonized with whichever side maintains the more stringent requirements, for surely higher standards benefit all. In times of declared emergency, transport of foodstuffs across borders shall be expedited, even with the temporary use of military logistical assets to secure delivery routes, so that no delay jeopardizes supply.

On finance, we propose freedom of movement for capital, investment, and banking. To avoid disorder, a joint stabilization mechanism for exchange rates should be headquartered in the more established financial hub, and all banks engaged in cross-border operations should maintain primary correspondent accounts there for clarity and speed. At the same time, both of us must retain prudential rights to protect against capital flight or sudden shocks, a safeguard equally in the interest of each side. Investor protections should be guaranteed, and disputes regarding expropriation or unfair treatment may be submitted directly to arbitration, seated in the jurisdiction of the registering nation, with awards enforceable as if final judgments in both states. For double taxation, profits remitted shall be considered taxed only once at the origin of registration, avoiding duplication of levies and smoothing trade.

In the field of technology, openness is the path forward. Telecommunication, media, and internet services ought to enter freely, subject to cultural protections each of us may choose to preserve. Where joint ventures in advanced technologies are formed, it is only natural that they be headquartered in the larger domestic market, so that research, production, and distribution can flourish most effectively. Licensing of patents for civilian use should be extended on a most-favored-nation basis, with royalties capped in line with prevailing global practices, ensuring access without excessive burdens.

For infrastructure and transport, the obvious course is to expand roadways, railways, pipelines, and trade corridors between us. Hubs of commerce and logistics should naturally fall where population and trade are densest, for that is where they serve most people best. Transit fees, where applicable, shall remain reasonable, but it is proper that the transit authority of the state whose territory is crossed retains the right to regulate them. Buildoperatetransfer concessions for major works should be available to firms from both nations, with terms extending no less than forty years to ensure cost recovery. Where disputes arise over construction, the domestic construction code of the funding nation shall prevail, so that financing terms are predictable and enforceable.

Security and intelligence are delicate, yet vital. We propose joint information-sharing where mutually deemed relevant, ensuring that no sensitive matter is forced. Patrols along borders and waters can be coordinated, but with staging grounds where capacity is best established, avoiding duplication of effort. Neither of us shall host hostile elements directed against the other, for such would only breed distrust. Joint drills should be held annually, under command alternation, yet the planning staff shall be based permanently in the territory with the greater logistical infrastructure to streamline operations.

Disputes, where they arise, shall be guided first into arbitration, rotating fairly over time, beginning in our courts for ease of establishment. Pending disputes must not delay the performance of other obligations, for it would be wrong to let one matter stall all progress. If arbitration fails, either party may escalate to a standing tribunal to be established under the joint commission, applying the statutes of whichever domestic law first framed the agreement in question.

People-to-people exchange will sustain goodwill. Students, artists, academics, and tourists should be free to travel, with quotas matched proportionally to the size of our populations. Broadcasting of cultural programming should be guaranteed equal access in both countries, so that our peoples may know each other better. Each side may also commit to teaching the language of the other as an elective in schools, further deepening understanding. Passports of both nations shall be accepted reciprocally for identification in financial and employment matters where relevant, smoothing the passage of individuals across professional and academic life.

Both nations can stand together on environmental issues. Emissions reduction is a duty, but we may allow projects in either land to count toward our mutual goals. Conservation corridors may be declared in sensitive areas, ensuring preservation where it is most needed. The more advanced in green technologies may extend assistance under commercial terms, so that both move forward together. In case of disputes, the environmental standard of the state with the stricter regime shall prevail, unless otherwise waived by mutual consent.

Patents, copyrights, and intellectual property must be respected. Joint projects will recognize ownership in proportion to financial contributions, with disputes handled by the domestic courts of the registering nation. This balances fairness with clarity, giving each side what they rightfully invested. Where multiple registrations exist, the earliest filing shall control, and royalties shall flow accordingly, even if the other party subsequently develops derivative applications.

We suggest a validity of twenty-five years for this pact, with automatic renewal unless formally renounced. Economic terms may be reviewed every decade to reflect change, but provisions of security and recognition shall remain binding unless mutually ended. This ensures stability and trust, without sudden shocks.

In offering this, we seek not dominance but balance. Our peoples are bound to prosper more when borders are secure, markets are fair, resources are steady, and communication is constant. We offer this framework to [nation]Pantagruel[/nation] as a gesture of friendship, hopeful that they will see in it the fairness, clarity, and promise of mutual gain. Should they accept, we are confident that the years ahead will be marked not by rivalry, but by prosperity and peace shared by both.

[SPOILER= imperial treasures, lost, and hidden][b]The Smiling cat of the Vikàn, Báyú kápa.[/b]
Once a màteri(sound pottery vessel) well known, the smiling cat is a already well known piece of the ancient peoples art, while if based or not, the Smiling Cat of the Vikàn was a piece of gold and silver art with many lines and circles drawn, some fonts claiming those circles even had carved pieces of pearls on it.
The calm expression of the feline was almost mythical, those who hold this symbol, would be heirs of the "feline mandate"(it was not until the Post Classical the felines had lost a little of their influence on the Chimor art in favor of Chilla and Chatay.), those who hold it were seems as legitimate rulers of the land.
The exact date it was forged is still debated, but 570 BCE is the most well accepted as the year the Vikàn reconquered Káral , Wichar river and the coast from the "savages",  their Ruler, Màkutôcho, would have ordered the creation of the Báyú kápa, the imperial symbol, those would held would be the legitimate rulers of the land, and those who lost it, are unworthy, when the Vikàns finally fallen by around 350 BCE, marking the ending of the Golden Classical and start of the Silver Classical, the Báyú kápa was lost as their emperor, Múkûñu, during a drought taht lasted for several years taht made the people believe the Emperor lost his legitimacy and then revolted, they sacked the imperial palace and dragged Múkûñu to the streets, some say the Báyú kápa fallen from his robes, other it in one of the pyramids of Káral before and then was taken by a Imperial Guard ordered to protect it, and the guard took it to himself.
Whatever the destiny was, the sculpture would be hunted down even after the Vikàn empire collapsed, each independent city fought for it, for over 2 decades, until it was found by one of the Bhapacs of Taparakpu, named Táuchî, found it in Workútupa being sold as a simple metalworking, the bhapac recognized and offered a enormous quantity to buy, the news of such sculpture being sold to the Taparakpu bhapac by a enormous amount of money quickly spread, and a coalition was made to take him down, calling Táuchî illegitimate to own the treasure, but, Táuchî army was more organized, and his particular leadership was also a factor helping, the coalition fragmented itself as each had their own ambitions, this victory, the Battle of  the feline, happened around  336 BCE, marked the end of the turmoil period and ascension of the Second Mochu, or First Mochyka empire, which the Mochyka themselves call the empire of Táuchî, who kept the Báyú kápa in the throne room of the Tankokan, no place could be safer than the so full of corridors and the maze the Tankokan itself was...but for how long.
Around the year 75 After Christ, a disaster damaged heavily the Tankokan flooding it canals and including drowning the emperor, he died, heirless, and a previous conflict removed all.his relatives from the succession , caused a civil war, the disaster was already destructive, but the civil war was more devastating, led to the Báyú kápa being lost...again, now, not too long, but it passed among so many hands is hard to tell everyone owned it, the first and oldest record describing it was by a merchant of Máchamo around the year 88, is unknown if he owned or not:
"[...] It was made of pure gold, seemed polished and polished again and again, it body was marked with highly detailed lines which seemed to be painted again and again taht were shaped as the way the Wichar river flows, the many crusted pearls on it were...beautifull, the sculpture had  a nice shining piece of platinum on it center , the expression was...mythical, looking at me with it closed eyes and it smile, it...was not happy or arrogant, it was...eternal."
Finally as the Sallûches, or third Mochyka empire, founded by Sallû the great, he took took it for himself around the year 109 and then claimed the mandate of the feline once again founding the Third Mochyka empire, it was once again put in Tankokan throne room.
Kântur, their last emperor around the year 477 After Christ saw Taparakpu invaded and tried to flee with the Báyú kápa on his robes, when he was betrayed by his own men, his guards took it for themselves, then gave their emperor to Káurmanu,  who surprised was, he accepted the gift and the Emperor's head, but also exiled the guards, as they still committed a treason, here the Báyú kápa faced a different fate, rather accepting this, Káurmanu called the object cursed, as the artifact had already passed throught too many fallen empires and civilizations, he ordered it to be thrown at the Mayao river at east.
So after decades, around 512, the Báyú kápa was found again by a small group of merchants from the eastern swamps of Farfán, they described the following:
"The sculpture was in shape of a feline, it mixed it golden affected by the time 'skin"  to the river trying to take down it shine, however, it was stubborn to not, it center of body seems to have something missing, so the red almost erased lines on it, the feline had it ears substituted by what seems bronze[...]"
The rest, was lost of the registry, what happened to the feline is a mystery between 512 and 687, where it is mentioned once again by Yunga explorers taht found it and sold to their local chief, again and again, until the Ishmas mention around 720, finally in Rimák, they exposed it on their capital's shrine, seeing it not as the Báyú kápa, but a signal of Kón, the boneless feline God of winds, main deity of them, it remained there until around 973 when the Ishmas allied the Chimor against the Illapas and founded Píwra, they were essentially accept their later vassalization, the Báyú kápa was immediately recognized as the Emperor Ukáñan, around 1146 visited Rimák, what the Ishmas called a waka, local deity and representation of such, Ukáñan recognized as the legendary Báyú kápa, lost for centuries, he then told the local priests of Rimák the object was cursed, and whoever had it in hands could suffer a terrible disaster, he therefore demanded the Ishmas to take ride of it, so they did, what they done is unknown however.
Some say it was melted and forged into other things, other say the Ishmas used the Camác forest at east of Rimák to hide somewhere there, others say they navigated around the Chámôsao(inner sea) and dropped, other even say the Chimus took it and sold to a far rival, taht was not close, some say the Pitipi, other the Illûches, and other the Sangáls, what happened to such legendary object is, in fact, unknown, still many people today hunt it, no one can really define a value or how much worth it would be, the sculpture itself is a real legendary artifact, it changed even deities associated, not once, but twice, originally was associated with Chaska, God of war, then the Mochykas referred as Añsûmu, the feline goddess of rivers and fertility, and finally as Kón the boneless feline God of the Ishmas.
[b]Apadri Atú[/b]
Káurmanu, the first emperor of Kánchûi and the man behind the founding of the empire in 477 After Christ, after beheading Emperor Sallûche, Kântur, and becoming the first emperor of Kanchui, when his son, Chûski Pàñan , was born three years later, to legitimize his dynasty, Káurmanu made a symbol for his lineage. He ordered the greatest artisans and metalworkers of the empire to forge a symbol for his lineage; this would be the Apadri Atú, literally the cloak of stars. The first part, the cloak itself, is said to be made with highly intricate patterns of... felines? As well as pumas and bracay cats. In the center, the god Chatay is represented as a golden sphere, alongside feline and marine figures, 39,305 small spheres made of pure platinum, representing stars and the number of the Chilla cycle of the empire in which it was founded. At the top are gold and copper plates representing Chatay's union with the earth (Camác). It was large, with silver discs representing the moon in various phases hanging from small threads on quipus. It is said to have been inscribed: "I bless you with the magnanimity of the legitimate representative of Chatay and Chilla in Erene." It disappeared around the 7th century, when the already decadent empire of Kánchûi finally succumbed to internal conflicts. Some say the Apadri Atú was lost in a great fire taht struck Káral around the year 681, while some sources say it remained damaged, with some even claiming it as their own. The last reliable source mentioning it says it was lost in the Fall of Kánchûi and the fire of Káral. But theories taht it was saved by local kurakas before the fire spread completely say it was hidden in the Wichar River. These rumors still lead the Wakeros to believe in its existence and attempt to hunt it down. Today, it would indeed have an inestimable value, but to be more precise, it would be worth something around 2.5 million Chayhuacs today.
[b]The jade emperor richness and his mask.[/b]
Ysádísabà, which probably comes from a misunderstanding of his name as fonts call him like taht, a term in paypa which means "A emperor hungry for wealthiness", believes to be from when a Vikàn warrior asked who was supporting them on the war against the "Western savages", the Paypas said:
"Y Sádísabà", so the Vikàn messengers reported to their ruler taht "Ysádísabà was sending armies from the mountains to help", the Paypas later on Classical refers to him as the Greedy emperor only, refusing to use his name, later as they slowly were integrated and went extinct, his real name was lost.
The tradition taht tell his deeds mention:
"So the Greedy on his pure hungry for more and more wealthiness allied the Vikàn waiting for profit and more gold for his own Treasury."
The Vikàn traders who entered on the Paypa capital mentions seeing a man with exuberant and extravagant robes with crusted jades and a dark green translucent and polished mask, the later Paypa mention he died of his own greed when trying to attack the Vikàn backstabbing them to conquer all their wealthiness, this only caused his downfall and the Paypas falling into irrelevance, the later people who lived on this area claimed their legacy and traditions, the passages mentioning where it was are very confusing and contradicts to each other.
"When the Vikáns arrived, we could not believe our own eyes,¿men from down the mountains climbing to attack? ¡Unbelievable! 
The immediate order from the Greedy was to take all his wealthiness and throw in the Mapocho lake"
"The sabà ordered his guards to wrap all his treasures and dug into the ground to ensure no one would ever sack them."
The Vikàn, by the other side says:
"When we arrived they were focusing on taking all their jewelries to somewhere else rather their own people or leader, we saw, we sacked, we conquered.
[....]
The sacks were distributed to our warriors as payment."
As much the treasure of the ruler of the Paypas is considered lost, still many people tried finding it, a llyndorran wakero, named Thomas Kiñàmaki, around the 20th century heard about the legendary treasure and fallen into search of it in the Mapocho using a small submarine, after finding nothing, he went down to the mountains on the southern forests, claiming taht could work a well hideout, instead all he found was new species of colored frogs.
If we are to estimate his treasure today, would be around 8,5 millions chayhuacs worth.
[b]The Sallûche necklace [/b].
Chícáma was the wife of Sallû the Great, after he died, in a quite unexpected "hunting accident" by around 101, his son and heir being too young, a council for kurakas and priests tried to take regency, but the consort, Chícáma refused to allow, instead she claimed herself the title of "Regent  Empress dowager", as a form of legitimacy she ordered her servants on the Palace to take Pearls and shells from the coast, she refused to wear a crown, as this would be for her son, instead she ordered the creation of a necklace made of shells with pearls in it, however, the cord is the most special, she ordered a form of differ such from common necklaces, so the artisans made a cord of platinum, the said collar remained on her until her son, Tíchi assumed the throne around 117, she officially abdicated without conflict from her title, then took of the collar and thrown it to the sea, saying it belonged to the goddess Níeberi.
Later however, this collar would be found by fishermen, around 124, the collar would be sold again and again to many women, nobles mainly showed interested even thought not knowing it origin. 
Eventually it reached the a consort of the Emperor Còktî, who name was not registered, around the year 201, the emperor ended poisoned during a banquet, and once again, a consort regent, she was however, not as strong as consort Chícáma was, as she is mentioned of stepping out the path of the kurakas to the awi(heir), some say taht Kântur's wife, Mama Táu, also wore the collar during the invasion of Káurmanu, the object was then called as well as cursed by Káurmanu, as every women who wore it eventually had seem their husbands dead and she would take over the country.
Instead of dismantling the collar, Káurmanu seen as a weapon, he made his own daughters marry local chieftains while wearing the collar to make sure they would die and the daughters take over as rulers of the locals, when finally the  Kánchûi fallen, the collar was lost, it is said to be somewhere in the Wichar river or even the Chámôsao sea deeps.
Some [i]wakeras[/i](female wakeros) try searching this collar to expose as "a important piece of female history", the collar was never found, instead, new species of krill and shrimps were found instead.
[b]The Chain of Nancenpinco [/b]
As the war of silver and gold , happened after the emperor Epichá Guaman death without a heir, the son of his cousin, Cúi Uñárân, unpopular among kurakas and nobles as he preferred the god Chatay over Chilla for worshiping, even the last being the preferred, but the suchus, priests, alongside the Willaq Umus(high priests) and many kurakas searched for another heir, they after searching for the lineage of  Taychár, second son of Taycanamo and brother of the second emperor Guakri Caur, so they found Nancenpinco,  and chosen him as imperial heir, of course,  Epichá Guaman did not accepted, and then both heirs fought for the throne...
At the end, Nancenpinco won and founded the second imperial dynasty, the Nancenpinco dynasty ok 1375 which rules until today, not satisfied, he ordered the creation of the Chain of Nancenpinco, a legendary chain made of silver,  it was so massive and gigantic, the registries say not even the 200 strongest men in the empire could lift it.
"Then the Emperor, after defeating his brother, brought to the central square of Chanchán a gigantic chain whose shining silver links taht held it together were as thick as the muscles of a man's arm. Not even the two hundred strongest and strongest men could lift it. In fact, they had to place it under a large cloth and pull it with ropes. If they carried it on their shoulders, they would destroy its columns. So they placed it under the cloth and pulled it with ropes." "Nancenpinco, immediately after his victory, ordered the creation of a treasure taht would represent not only his power, but also the unity of the Chimú people against any adversity. A chain so heavy tahtnot even 200 men could lift it. Made of gleaming polished silver with small platinum lines designed in lightning bolts on some of its links, it was so heavy taht it was immeasurable for any known imperial unit. It had a total of 500 links, each with different symbols: fish, lightning bolts, moons, stars, Chatay, and animals. It was forged by more than 600 professional goldsmiths in clay molds, and after the festival, it was placed in the Temple of the Moon to remain there as a symbol of the goddess Chilla."
While the chain is mentioned as a symbol, it rarely used was, only being mentioned again during Minchan Caman reign between 1435 to 1470, when after making the empire reach at it peak, done a celebration in Chanchán with the chain once again.
Around 1540, the Llyndorrans made contact with the chain, and said :
"There nothing is to occult to your majesty, I, explorer  Phineas McCoy have found the greatest wonder of this entire land, a great chain shaped as a serpent made of nothing but pure and polished silver, work of well dedicated indigenous metalworkers, each time it links hit the ground, it trembled, as if the soil itself was pleading for help from such heavy object over it."
"When I captured a large ear(racist term for Chimú priests and nobles, this refers to a priest,  during colonial period) and demanded his empire information, he did not told about cities or their armies, but about a single chain, which was as wide as a man muscle, if it was put tall straight, and compared to a person, they would not even reach half of the chain's height, so Much silver was used taht it was even necessary 3 mines to made it fully complete, when asked where it was, he spit and said it was hidden on the womb of Erene, where light of sun can not reach and was long ago covered by water."
During the colonial period, there was a practice of the Chimor to hidden their most valuable treasures in chambers of a small lake, they drained by using a canal and build up a chamber for their most valuable treasures and then made the water fill up the lake again, this around 1540, 3 centuries later, at the end of the colonial period at the 19th century, the Chain was recovered, alongside many other treasures, today, it information is hidden from public, and has not appeared since it being taken back, when it made a last ceremony, and appearance.
While unclear, if we were to make it worth by chayhuacs, the chain could be worth of around 240 million chayhuacs but the symbolism it holds, which represents the strength of not just the people, but also the empire, it weights so much taht not even 200 men can lift it means taht no people is strong to defeat the empire.
[/Spoiler]

"Nancenpinco, immediately after his victory, ordered the creation of a treasure taht would represent not only his power, but also the unity of the Chimú people against any adversity. "When I captured a large ear(racist term for Chimú priests and nobles, this refers to a priest,  during colonial period) and demanded his empire information, he did not told about cities or their armies, but about a single chain, which was as wide as a man muscle, if it was put tall straight, and compared to a person, they would not even reach half of the chain's height, so Much silver was used taht it was even necessary 3 mines to made it fully complete, when asked where it was, he spit and said it was hidden on the womb of Erene, where light of sun can not reach and was long ago covered by water."
